title: orphaned-gpu-sockets-by-pool-2025-11-18
body:
Sheet: Orphaned GPU sockets and idle pockets by cluster/pool (investigation)

Purpose:
Quick triage sheet to identify pools and clusters with unexpectedly low active allocation but non-zero kernel-level GPU socket activity — i.e., GPUs present on hosts but not attached to active inference instances (suspected orphaned sockets from crash/reboot sequences or daemon mismanagement). Use this as input for capacity reclamation and remediation runbook.

Notes to self:
- This is an exploratory export mixed from cluster metrics and host-level GPU socket counters (nvidia-smi sockets and runtime-agent heartbeat).
- Values are sampled daily at 02:00 UTC to catch off-peak anomalies.
- ‚Orphaned sockets‘ = total_gpus - active_vms - reserved_for_preserved (where reserved_for_preserved is from reservation tags) minus expected idle buffer.
- Flag threshold: orphaned_sockets >= 2 AND avg_util_pct < 5% for 3 consecutive samples.

Table (recent 7-day snapshot):
Date,Cluster,Pool,Region,total_gpus,active_vms,avg_util_pct,p95_util_pct,idle_gpus,orphaned_sockets,notes
2025-11-12,eu-west-1-cluster-A,preemptible-medium,eu-west-1,48,36,6.2,18,8,4,bursting during morning traffic, some hosts show stale driver load
2025-11-13,eu-west-1-cluster-A,preemptible-medium,eu-west-1,48,34,5.1,14,10,6,two reboot events recorded around 01:45 UTC
2025-11-14,us-east-1-cluster-B,dedicated-high,us-east-1,128,122,74.5,92,2,0,steady; no orphan signals
2025-11-15,us-west-2-cluster-C,spot-small,us-west-2,96,61,8.9,26,35,19,high idle pockets after load spike drained; long tail of terminated VMs
2025-11-16,ap-southeast-1-cluster-D,reserved-medium,ap-southeast-1,64,44,11.3,29,12,3,one host with driver mismatch (ticket), possible mismatch between agent and kernel
2025-11-17,eu-west-1-cluster-A,preemptible-medium,eu-west-1,48,33,4.8,12,11,7,orphaned sockets persist; investigate agent restart sequence
2025-11-18,us-west-2-cluster-C,spot-small,us-west-2,96,59,7.4,21,37,21,post-eviction churn; tasks not reaping device mappings

High-level observations:
- Spot pools (us-west-2-cluster-C) show the largest correlated orphaned pockets. Hypothesis: rapid VM termination/eviction leaves GPU device mappings in a state where runtime-agent doesn't reattach and host drivers still report socket availability but K8sCRI hasn't reclaimed properly.
- eu-west preemptible pool also showing persistent small pockets across multiple days — likely agent crash or version skew around 2025-11-13 (see linked infra-ops#431).
- Dedicated pools maintain expected low orphan counts; suggests problem is eviction/termination related rather than hardware.

Quick remediation suggestions (prioritized):
1) Patch runtime-agent to add a watchdog at agent startup that forces GPU device re-scan and clears stale /dev/nvidia* references. Short-term rollout to spot/ preemptible pools only. (PR: runtime#762).
2) Add a Kubernetes finalizer/cleanup job that runs on node Terminating state to ensure CUDA socket teardown. Schedule as a DaemonSet with low burst.
3) Capacity reclamation script: nightly job to identify hosts with orphaned_sockets >= 4 for >24h and cordon + drain + reboot, with automated alert to on-call. Use a soft-drain first to avoid user impact.
4) Instrumentation: add a metric orphaned_socket_count exported via node-exporter and create a Grafana alert (threshold: 5 sockets for 6h) and an email + PagerDuty escalation path for infra.

Open questions / data gaps:
- Are any customer workloads affected (errors, longer queue times)? Need to cross-check with request queue growth per-route (link to product telemetry).
- exact mapping between 'idle_gpus' and 'orphaned_sockets' differs by driver version — need to include driver version in future exports.
- how many callbacks from kubelet during termination are lost? correlate with kubelet logs (ticket GHD-1284)

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Miguel Sanchez: produce a per-host log extract for us-west-2 spot pool (due 2025-11-20).
- Evan Liu: prototype runtime-agent re-scan in staging, open PR for review (target 2025-11-22).
- Priya Narayanan: create Grafana panel + alert and add to runbook (target 2025-11-21).
- Aisha Patel (me): run nightly reclamation smoke run in sandbox and report cost delta (target 2025-11-24).

Appendix: quick sampling commands used to generate sheet
- host-level socket dump: sudo /usr/local/bin/gpu-socket-dump --format=csv --since=24h
- active VM mapping: kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}: {.metadata.name}\n' | sort
- reconciliation heuristic snippet: orphaned = total_gpus - active_vms - reserved - expected_idle_buffer

References:
- infra-ops#431 (linked): recent node agent crashes in eu-west-1 around 2025-11-13
- GHD-1284: request to collect kubelet teardown logs for termination path
- runtime PR 762: early-stage re-scan implementation (staging)

Free-form notes (scratch):
- We should consider an automated reclaim where orphaned_sockets > 10 and host CPU usage < 5% for 2h — safe to reboot automatically in spot pools.
- Need to check whether reserved_for_preserved incorrectly counts leftover reservations from completed jobs (noticed in us-west-2 logs).
- Customer impact threshold: if orphaned sockets cause >=12% reduction in effective capacity for a pool during a 1h window, trigger immediate mitigation runbook.

End of sheet.
